description: Patient lives alone in a single-story home with 2 cats
presentation: A 59-year-old woman with end-stage renal disease who underwent a deceased-donor kidney transplant a few years ago has a remote history of an unprovoked, isolated subsegmental pulmonary embolism in the right lower lobe, now 3.5 years ago. She lives alone in a single-story home with 2 cats. She completed roughly three months of apixaban at that time, without hematology follow-up or additional surveillance, and has remained off anticoagulation with no new clotting events. Her routine labs, including serial complete blood counts, metabolic panels, and a recent ferritin of 1059 ng/mL, are stable. She has no ongoing signs or family history of venous thromboembolism or active malignancy on age-appropriate screening. Should the patient resume indefinite anticoagulation given the unprovoked pulmonary embolism?
